title: Areas of Strategic Visibility: Disability Bias in Biometrics
extended_summary:
This paper is a position statement responding to a request for information on biometrics, with a focus on how biometric systems can harm or exclude disabled people. It argues that accessibility problems are not limited to algorithmic accuracy; they also arise from inaccessible interfaces, biased datasets, unsuitable configuration, and systems that encode ableist assumptions. The paper frames disability in terms of systemic barriers and emphasizes that equitable biometric use requires moving beyond narrow notions of fairness or inclusion toward agency, control, and disability justice.

The paper does not study an educational intervention or a learner population. Instead, it synthesizes risks and opportunities across biometric recognition and inference, including identification, access control, diagnosis, public safety, and workplace monitoring. It highlights how disabled people may be misrecognized, excluded, or pathologized by biometric systems, and why data collection, validation, governance, and transparency processes must involve disabled communities from design through deployment.

Its main conclusion is that biometrics should never be treated as sufficient for disability identification or service eligibility, and that stronger regulation, accessible design, participatory development, and interpretability/correctability are required. The authors argue that without these guardrails, biometric technologies can amplify discrimination and produce serious harms, even when framed as fairness-improving or beneficial tools.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI/chatbot systems based on large language models or similar generative methods.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper does not evaluate a reading or literacy tool; it is a disability-bias position statement about biometrics and AI governance, with only incidental references to AI systems such as HireVue and biometric recognition technologies.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a position statement / policy response rather than an empirical study. It contains no direct evaluation of an AI tool on K-12 reading or literacy outcomes, no comparison group, and no effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no reported intervention effect on student outcomes, so impact on reading or literacy cannot be assessed from this paper.
